title: Canonical module-to-abelian inverse-image comparison is invertible
statement: Let $i:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $\Lambda$ a commutative ring. Let $J$ be a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site of $Y$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Write $U_X,U_Y$ for the functors forgetting to abelian sheaves. For the inverse-image and direct-image adjunctions [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-direct-image], the abelian adjoint of $U_Y(\eta^{\mathrm{Mod}}_J):U_YJ\to i_*U_X(i^{-1}_{\mathrm{Mod}}J)$ is an isomorphism $i^{-1}_{\mathrm{Ab}}U_YJ\xrightarrow{\sim}U_X(i^{-1}_{\mathrm{Mod}}J)$. This is the particular canonical comparison determined by the module adjunction unit, not merely existence of some isomorphism.

proof.text: Write the inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] as left Kan extension followed by sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. The functor forgetting a module to its additive group preserves colimits and limits. Mathlib Functor.leftKanExtensionCompIsoOfPreserves and sheafComposeNatIso therefore give an isomorphism e from the abelian inverse image of the underlying sheaf to the underlying module inverse image.

Naturality of the sheafification unit and sheafComposeNatTrans_fac show that the composite of the abelian sheafification unit with e is the inverse Kan-extension comparison followed by the underlying module sheafification unit. The factorization leftKanExtensionCompIsoOfPreserves_inv_fac then shows that the abelian adjoint of e is the underlying module adjunction unit; direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] commutes with forgetting because it is restriction of presheaves. Apply the injective adjunction hom equivalence: e is the displayed canonical map, so that map is an isomorphism.
